free_prompt.title: Sort Inbox by Priority
free_prompt.objective: Sort the user's Gmail inbox by tagging emails with "Urgent" in the subject line with a "Priority" label.
free_prompt.credentials: [User provides Gmail login email and password]
free_prompt.preconditions: User is logged into Gmail via the web interface (https://mail.google.com). A "Priority" label exists in Gmail (if not, create it).
steps: Open a browser and navigate to https://mail.google.com.
If not logged in, enter [user-provided email] in the email field, click "Next," enter [user-provided password], and click "Sign In."
On the Gmail homepage, locate the search bar at the top of the page.
In the search bar, type: Urgent -in:spam -in:trash.
Press the "Enter" key to execute the search.
Verify that the search results show emails with "Urgent" in the subject line (exclude spam/trash).
On the left sidebar, locate the "Labels" section (scroll down if needed).
If "Priority" label does not exist, click "Create new label" at the bottom of the Labels section, type "Priority" in the dialog box, and click "Create."
Above the search results, click the checkbox to select all visible emails (up to 50 per page).
Click the "Labels" icon (a tag shape) in the toolbar above the email list.
In the dropdown, select "Priority" and click "Apply."
If more than 50 emails are found, click "Select all conversations that match this search" at the top of the results, then repeat steps 10-11.
Confirm the "Priority" label is applied by checking the left sidebar for the labeled emails.
error_handling: If login fails, notify user via email: "Gmail login failed. Check credentials: [user-provided email]."
If search returns no results, notify user: "No emails with 'Urgent' found in inbox."
If "Priority" label creation fails, notify user: "Failed to create Priority label. Create manually and retry."
free_prompt.output_format: Email user: "Gmail inbox sorted. [X] emails tagged with Priority label. Check Gmail: https://mail.google.com."

free_prompt.title: Auto-Fill Daily Report
free_prompt.objective: Automatically populate a daily report template with data from various sources.
free_prompt.credentials: [User provides Google account login email and password]
free_prompt.preconditions: User has a Google Sheets template for daily reporting. User has access to the data sources needed for the report.
steps: Open a browser and navigate to https://sheets.google.com.
If not logged in, enter [user-provided email] in the email field, click "Next," enter [user-provided password], and click "Sign In."
Locate and open the daily report template from the Google Sheets homepage.
Click on cell A1 to begin the data entry process.
Enter today's date in the designated date field (typically near the top of the report).
Navigate to the data source tabs or external sources as needed.
Copy the required data from the source.
Paste the data into the appropriate cells in the report template.
Repeat steps 6-8 for all required data points.
Once all data is entered, check for any calculation errors or missing information.
Format the report as needed (adjust column widths, apply conditional formatting, etc.).
Click on "File" > "Download" > "PDF Document" to create a PDF version of the report.
Click on "Share" in the top-right corner to share the report with stakeholders.
error_handling: If login fails, notify user: "Google Sheets login failed. Check credentials: [user-provided email]."
If template cannot be found, notify user: "Daily report template not found. Please check the template name or create a new one."
If data sources are unavailable, notify user: "Unable to access data sources. Please check permissions and try again."
free_prompt.output_format: Email user: "Daily report completed and saved at [Google Sheets URL]. PDF version downloaded to your computer."

free_prompt.title: Channel Message Poster
free_prompt.objective: Create and post formatted messages to multiple Slack channels efficiently.
free_prompt.credentials: [User provides Slack workspace URL and login credentials]
free_prompt.preconditions: User has posting permissions in the target Slack channels. User has the message content prepared.
steps: Open a browser and navigate to [user's Slack workspace URL] or open the Slack desktop app.
If not logged in, enter [user-provided email] and [user-provided password], then click "Sign In."
Once in Slack, click on the "+" icon next to "Drafts" in the left sidebar.
In the new draft area, compose your message with the desired formatting.
Use Markdown for basic formatting: *bold* for bold text, _italic_ for italics, and `code` for code snippets.
For more advanced formatting, click the "Aa" formatting button in the message composer.
Add any necessary links, mentions (@username), or channel mentions (#channel).
If including attachments, click the "+" icon in the message composer and select the file to upload.
Once the message is composed, save it as a draft by clicking "Save as draft."
Navigate to the first target channel in the left sidebar.
Click in the message field, then click the "..." menu and select "Your drafts."
Select your saved draft, which will populate the message field.
Review the message, make any channel-specific adjustments, then click "Send."
Repeat steps 10-13 for each additional target channel.
error_handling: If login fails, notify user: "Slack login failed. Check workspace URL and credentials."
If user lacks posting permissions, notify user: "You don't have permission to post in [channel name]. Request access from a workspace admin."
If draft saving fails, notify user: "Unable to save draft. Try copying your message text to a local document as backup."
free_prompt.output_format: Notification in Slack: "Message successfully posted to [X] channels: [list of channel names]."

free_prompt.title: Caption Generator
free_prompt.objective: Generate engaging captions for Instagram posts to increase engagement and followers.
free_prompt.preconditions: User has photos/videos ready to post. User knows their target audience and post theme.
steps: Open the Instagram app on your mobile device or navigate to https://www.instagram.com on a web browser.
Log in with [user-provided username] and [user-provided password].
Click the "+" icon (mobile) or the "Create" button (web) to start creating a new post.
Select the photo or video you want to post.
Apply filters or edits as desired, then click "Next."
On the caption screen, consider your post's purpose (promotional, educational, entertaining, etc.).
Draft a caption that includes: a hook (first line to grab attention), main content (2-3 sentences about the image/video), and a call-to-action (question or instruction).
Add 3-5 relevant hashtags that mix popular tags (#love, #photooftheday) with niche tags specific to your content.
Include emojis strategically to break up text and add personality (2-3 emojis maximum).
If tagging other accounts, click "Tag People" and add relevant accounts.
If adding a location, click "Add Location" and select the appropriate place.
Review your caption for spelling/grammar errors and ensure it aligns with your brand voice.
Click "Share" to publish your post with the engaging caption.
error_handling: If login fails, notify user: "Instagram login failed. Check credentials or try again later due to possible temporary restrictions."
If post upload fails, notify user: "Unable to upload media. Check file format (JPG, PNG for images; MP4 for videos) and size (maximum 100MB for videos)."
If hashtags aren't working, notify user: "Instagram may be limiting hashtag use. Try reducing the number of hashtags or check if any are banned."
free_prompt.output_format: Instagram post published with optimized caption. Analytics available in Instagram Insights after 24 hours.

free_prompt.title: Video Caption Generator
free_prompt.objective: Create attention-grabbing captions for TikTok videos to maximize views and engagement.
free_prompt.preconditions: User has recorded and edited their TikTok video. User understands their target audience.
steps: Open the TikTok app on your mobile device.
Log in with [user-provided username] and [user-provided password].
Tap the "+" button at the bottom of the screen to create a new video.
Upload your pre-recorded video or record a new one in the app.
Edit your video with effects, filters, and sounds as desired, then tap "Next."
On the caption screen, start with a hook that creates curiosity or promises value (e.g., "This hack changed my life...").
Keep the caption short and punchy (40-80 characters is ideal).
Include 1-2 trending hashtags related to your content (check the Discover page for current trends).
Add 1-2 niche hashtags specific to your content category.
Include the hashtag #fyp or #foryoupage to increase chances of appearing on the For You Page.
Add 2-3 relevant emojis to make your caption visually appealing.
If applicable, tag relevant accounts by typing "@" followed by their username.
Review your caption for typos and clarity, then tap "Post" to publish your TikTok.
error_handling: If login fails, notify user: "TikTok login failed. Check credentials or try again later."
If video upload fails, notify user: "Video upload failed. Ensure your video is between 15-60 seconds and under 287.6MB."
If hashtags aren't working, notify user: "Some hashtags may be restricted. Try alternative hashtags or reduce the total number."
free_prompt.output_format: TikTok video published with optimized caption. Check TikTok Analytics after 24-48 hours to measure performance.
